description: Finite-sample quantiles of the ADF t statistics tau1 (no deterministic terms, trend 'n'), tau2 (constant, 'c') and tau3 (constant and trend, 'ct') under the unit-root null, as response surfaces in T (length of the series) and k (lagged differences). Decision D21 of the specification.
model: q_p(T, k) = intercept[p] + slopes[k][p][1] / T + slopes[k][p][2] / T^2 + slopes[k][p][3] / T^3, with T = N + k + 1 (N the effective number of observations)

usage.p_value: F(stat) = pnorm of the linear interpolation of qnorm(probs) against the quantiles at the statistic (monotone, exact at the tabulated probabilities); p = F for this lower-tail test. Beyond the quantiles do not extrapolate: report the bound 0.001 (stat <= q[0.001]) or 0.999 (stat >= q[0.999])
usage.outside_design: use k = min(k, max(k)); use T = max(T, Tmin[k]) from design; never extrapolate; warn
usage.phillips_perron: Z_tau uses the k = 0 surface at T = N + 1

statistic: t ratio of y_{t-1} in the OLS regression of diff(y)_t on the deterministic terms (none, constant, or constant and t), y_{t-1} and k lagged differences, t = k+2..T

source.simulation: driftless random walk, N(0,1) innovations; T = 20..1000, k = 0..min(12, Schwert kmax) and 13..21 for T >= 150; 40 experiments x 10,000 replications per T, all k on the same paths; fit on T >= 25 by WLS with weights 1/se^2
source.validation: out-of-sample size at 5%: 4.7-5.4% (data-raw/tau_validate.R); at k = 0 within 0.008 of MacKinnon (2010) critical values

reference_values.note: R unitroottools 0.3.3: critical values at 1/5/10% and p-value of `stat`; an implementation reading this file should reproduce them to 1e-12
